[spoiler=Oceanice Expansion]Oceanice Republic launched a calculated invasion of its smaller neighbor to seize control of mineral-rich lands and to expand Oceanices industrial and ideological frontier. Exksian, politically divided and militarily outdated, stood little chance against the highly upgraded and disciplined Oceanice military. Within months, key territories had fallen, and by the end of the year, the Exksian capital and the vital province of Resutions had been seized. No treaty was signed; Exksian sovereignty was simply erased.
In June 1941, Oceanice formalized this conquest with the passage of the Territorial Unification and Protection Act, officially annexing the entirety of Exksian territory into the Oceanice Republic. The former nation was dissolved and redesignated as Unified Administrative Zone 4, or UAZ-4. From the beginning, this was no mere military occupation. Oceanice intended permanent, irreversible integration. The Expsian language, cultural expressions, and political history were banned under a sweeping Cultural Rectification Decree. Cities were renamed. The old flags were outlawed. Schools were restructured to teach Oceanice-approved history. Over time, entire generations grew up never knowing Exksian as anything other than a number on a central governments map.
The annexed region was rapidly industrialized. Through forced collectivization, factory construction, and state seizure of all major land and assets, UAZ-4 became a massive production zone serving the Oceanice core economy. Mines in Resutions fueled Oceanices steel and nuclear development programs. Rural farmland was cleared to construct mega-furnaces, power stations, and military testing grounds. Indigenous populations, particularly non-human ethnic groups such as the Avlue, were uprooted, confined to labor colonies, and forcibly resettled. Oceanice officials described this process as integration, but in reality, it was a colonial enterprise masked by bureaucratic language.
Among the most brutal aspects of Oceanice rule was its systemic racial hierarchy. Through a series of legislative decrees between 1942 and the early 1970s, non-humans were reclassified as sub-citizens. The Genetic Distinction Clause stripped them of legal protections. The Tiered Identity Act enforced racial segregation through internal passports and biometric ID tags. Movement was restricted, entire cities were closed to non-human entry, and access to education and healthcare was diminished or outright denied. Most egregiously, Oceanice implemented reproductive control programs in UAZ-4, forcibly sterilizing thousands under the guise of population optimization. Camps such as Facility 12-B became infamous for experimentation and abuse, with survivors emerging decades later with broken bodies and no legal recourse.
Despite overwhelming repression, resistance took root early. In the 1950s, the  Avlue Underground emerged as a decentralized but determined network of fighters, teachers, smugglers, and spiritual leaders. Armed resistance flared throughout the 1960s, including strikes, bombings, and sabotage operations aimed at Oceanice supply lines. While briefly effective, these efforts were met with overwhelming retaliation. As a result, the entire towns were razed, and counterinsurgency forces of the Secret Sereckist EnforceOceanices brutal internal security wing. Conducted mass arrests, disappearances, and information blackouts.
In the 1980s and 1990s, the struggle evolved. Activists shifted toward cultural preservation and encrypted communication. Songs, poems, and clandestine schools became tools of defiance. International attention briefly focused on the region after leaks of sterilization programs reached foreign media outlets in the early 2000s. Yet geopolitical interests prevailed. Oceanices rare minerals, especially those critical for global energy and weaponry, ensured that no sanctions were ever enforced. The world turned its gaze elsewhere, and the system remained intact.
Today, more than eighty years after the annexation, UAZ-4 remains firmly under Oceanice control. No referendum has ever been held. Governors are appointed by the central regime, not elected. Infrastructure, though advanced, primarily serves industrial transport and military logistics. Non-human populations are still subject to travel restrictions, surveillance drones, and regular behavioral compliance checks by the S.S.E. Schools in Avlue communities operate under heavily censored curricula. Speaking Avlue dialects in public can still lead to administrative detention. Dissidents continue to disappear. Officially, Oceanice refers to UAZ-4 as a fully integrated industrial region of national unity, yet the reality is far different.[/spoiler]

[b][i]KAAGANIKA ANNOUNCES CHANGE TO MILITARY DOCTRINE AND STRENGTHENS FURRIES RIGHTS[/i][/b]

[spoiler=RP][i]A man sits at his home watching television. While scrolling through channels, one of the programs catches his eye. General Odhoga is at his desk, talking to the camera with seemingly important news.[/i]

Good afternoon, great people of Kaaganika. Some of you may be aware of the current situation regarding the furry population of Erene. They have recently been suffering much hardships under some regimes such as [nation]Oceanice Republic[/nation], and we hold much prayers and hope for their safety and, hopefully, recovery.

We are now here to announce a big change in the inner workings of our military. The furry community and population within Kaaganika are now allowed to register and join in every given department of the military.

[i]Odhoga stands up and walks to another room, with the camera following suit. Odhoga sits down and the camera moves to include him and a furry sitting for a meeting. The furry, who was a native Kaaganikan antelope, was Aparu Nsuso, and was a leading figure for furries rights, particularly in West Shamat, and his movement had gained much traction in Kaaganika. The two sat across from each other and began discussions on live television.[/i]

[b]ODHAGA:[/b] Good afternoon, sir. I felt we needed this meeting to discuss on the status of furries rights in Kaaganika.

[b]APARU:[/b] Yes, quite. The fact that you and the government here are willing to work with me here is a great honor, and I hope we can reach an agreement here.

[i]The two reach to shake hands, and a flurry of camera images of the two are taken. Much debating and banter is taken between the two, and the two grew to be quite accustomed to each other during the meeting.[/i]

[i]Eventually, the two shook hands once again, smiles on their face, with the signing of a deal for furries rights in Kaaganika. Odhoga was to propose and protect the addition of a constitutional amendment to officially recognize furries as an equal people. Whether this comes to succeed, we need only wait and find out.[/i]
[/spoiler]
